text:
Maria: quick q — planning to expose per-customer quota overrides via runtime-config. what's the safest rollout pattern to avoid cross-tenant routing mixups?
Sam: are these overrides just config values or also route selectors? if the selector isn't sticky we could send requests to the wrong pool. :eyes:
Maria: both — override + selector. example payload i mocked: ```json
{
  "feature": "quota_override",
  "targets": [{
    "customer_id": "cust-123",
    "quota": 10000
  }],
  "rollout": {
    "pct": 10
  }
}```
Josh: telemetry gating is critical. emit a `config.change.errors` and `routing.mismatch.rate` metric for the first hour and auto-alert if either spikes >0.5%.
Emily: console UX: show a preview of "impacted routes" and an easy rollback button. also show which model/pool mapping will change. users need a dry-run toggle.
Ben: proposal: enforce a `shard_selector` field in the API that binds target->shard key, validate server-side. add a dry-run mode that only simulates routing for 1% sample for 30 minutes before full rollout.
Alice: also add `owned_by` metadata and require the team to add a safety contact so we don't accidentally apply tenant-wide overrides. and a global kill-switch flag.
Sam: +1 on `shard_selector`. can we make the selector a lambda? or at least a named key like `customer_id` or `region` to avoid arbitrary code in config.
Ben: named key only. no inline code. then runtime can guarantee placement.
Josh: add metrics: `rollout.progress` (tagged: flag, pct, env, impacted_routes) and `routing.sticky_failures`. those let SRE trigger canary aborts.
Maria: thinking about rollout automation: 1) validate schema 2) dry-run 1% for 30m 3) produce telemetry report 4) canary to 10% 5) conditional auto-increase if no regressions.
Emily: for the UI, show a "telemetry gate" step where users can require X minutes and Y threshold for key metrics. default to 30m / 0.5% regress.
Ben: for implementation we need: API change (new `shard_selector` field + `dry_run` flag), runtime support to honor selector and simulate routing, and a telemetry pipeline filter to tag sample traffic. I'll own the API + runtime glue.
Sam: small nit: make sure quota checks still happen at tokenization layer — don't let routing flip change enforcement order.
Alice: we should also add an audit log entry with before/after route mapping and a checksum of config so we can detect drift.
Maria: i'll open a PR with schema & docs. will include example curl: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/runtime-config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"feature":"quota_override","shard_selector":"customer_id","targets":[{"customer_id":"cust-123","quota":10000}],"rollout":{"pct":1},"dry_run":true}'
```
Ben: can you add a note to the PR about console gating? i'll wire the backend. @Emily can you do the mock?
Emily: yep i'll mock the telemetry-gate UI tiles this afternoon. :+1:
Josh: one more ask: add a short-circuit in the runtime to prefer `owned_by` team pools when present. that reduces blast radius.
Sam: agree. also add a test case in integration: simulate selector missing -> ensure config rejected.
deploy-bot: deploy started for branch config/schema-shard-guard (sha: a1b2c3). ETA 2m.
Maria: thanks all — i'll ping again once PR is up. Ben/Emily/Josh/Sam if you can review fast that'd be great. :rocket:
